appOverview: Corrector de Proyectos is a web application for vocational education (FP) teachers in Spain to manage and grade end-of-year student projects using a rubric-based scoring system. Teachers create rubrics per module, assign students to group projects (1–3 members), and grade each rubric item by selecting one of five quality levels whose values auto-sum to a final score. Administrators manage the system catalog (legislaciones, ciclos, módulos, profesorado). A restricted Tutor role can only view and download grade reports as PDF. The application enforces strict data privacy: student real names are stored separately from the anonymised identifiers used throughout the UI.

globalRules: All table filters are reactive text inputs with 300ms debounce; the table updates automatically as the user types without pressing any button.
In the correction screen, selecting a grade level for a rubric item auto-saves asynchronously to the DB; no explicit save button exists.
All rubric editable cells (item name and grade values) auto-save on blur; no explicit rubric save button exists.

Deleting any entity with dependencies is blocked; a warning message is shown and the deletion is prevented until all dependencies are resolved. Cascade order: Legislacion → Ciclos → Modulos → Proyectos/Alumnos.
Editing a row in any table activates inline editing directly in the row; no modal is opened for edit operations.
On first login with the default password '12345678', the user must change their password on the login screen before being redirected to their role home.
After 3 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is locked and 'Póngase en contacto con el Administrador' is displayed; only the admin can unlock accounts.

There is exactly one admin account in the system (username: 'Admin', default password: '12345678'). The admin first-login flow allows one retry on password mismatch; on second mismatch, user is redirected to login without account lockout.
Student real names are not stored in the main alumnos table; only anonymised identifiers (e.g. JJ499) are visible. Real names are stored in a separate high-security table linked by identifier.
After any successful save operation, the associated table refreshes by reading from the DB; no optimistic client-side insertion is performed.
Forms are not cleared automatically after saving; the form remains available for a new entry while the table reloads.
The academic year is represented as a single integer corresponding to the course start year (e.g. 2025 for the 2025-2026 academic year).
A student can belong to only one project at a time; students already assigned to a project do not appear in the alumno selection list when creating a new project.
Each module has exactly one rubric that applies to all its projects.
Grade report output format is PDF — not Excel and not the browser's print dialog.
The final grade formula is: nota_final = Σ(nota_modulo_i × horas_modulo_i / horas_totales_ciclo). A student with 'Excelente' on all items in all modules obtains exactly 10.
All rubric items must be graded for each alumno before a correction is considered complete; a warning is shown if the professor tries to navigate away with ungraded items.
All alumnos in a project must have all items graded before the project correction is marked complete.
A professor can re-correct an alumno at any time by selecting a different grade level; the new grade overwrites the previous one with no confirmation required.
Select inputs in creation/edit modals use <select> for fields with closed value lists (ciclo, legislacion, modulo, alumnos); free-text inputs are used only for open-ended fields (name, identifier).
